title: Anticipatory KV diffusion and decode gang scheduler to smooth prefill-decode handoffs
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: tail latency spikes and prefill misses remain a significant cost for interactive workloads where short prefill windows meet variable decode bursts. This PR introduces an anticipatory "KV diffusion" seeding layer plus a decode "gang" scheduler to reduce prefill misses and kernel churn at the prefill->decode handoff. In practice the two features work together: KV diffusion proactively seeds lightweight KV entries across co-scheduled microbatches based on prefix similarity and recent hot-key statistics; the gang scheduler co-schedules decodes that are likely to share kernel footprints and KV items so warmups and kernel launches are amortized. Key design points: 1) Probabilistic seeding: a bounded, asynchronous background task 'kv_diffuser' copies small delta-key sets to cached shards using a capped budget to avoid overwhelming memory. 2) Affinity scoring: we compute a stable affinity metric from prefix n-gram overlap, sequence-length bucket, and model-arch fingerprint; affinity drives the gang formation. 3) Kernel-aware co-scheduling: scheduler queries a small kernel-characteristic map and attempts to align decodes with compatible kernels to prevent back-to-back kernel reinitialization. 4) Safety knobs: per-customer diffusion budget (kv.diffusion.budget), per-pool gang_size, and an opt-out tag for privacy-sensitive workloads. Implementation summary: added a lightweight kv/kv_diffusion.* module, extended scheduler with a gang orchestrator (runtime/scheduler/gang_scheduler.cc), exposed two runtime flags and a telemetry set for prefill-miss-rate, kv.diffusion_hits, gang_coalesces. Backwards compatibility: features are gated behind runtime flags and default to off for Dedicated/Private until canary proves stable. Testing and CI: unit tests for diffusion heuristics and scheduler invariants, integration tests exercising prefill->decode handoff across mixed length loads, and a deterministic microbenchmark harness. Benchmarks: on our internal latency lab with seq_len=64 interactive traces we observed median end-to-end latency improvement of 7.6% and 95th percentile reduction of 11.2% for mixed-burst workloads; prefill miss-rate dropped ~36% for high locality traces. Rollout plan: feature flag -> canary (5% traffic on hosted) -> 25% -> full; create automatic rollback if kv.diffusion_hits > 0.8*prefill_count or if tail latency regresses by >5%. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-1209) [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] bench harness [x] telemetry added [x] docs snippet for new knobs [x] rollout plan. Related: builds on prior prefill windowing improvements but uses a different mechanism focused on proactive seeding and kernel co-scheduling rather than aggressive chunking.

comments: Kenji Saito: Overall this is promising; please add more comments on the probabilistic budget math and a small safety guard to early-stop diffusion if memory usage spikes.
Aisha Patel: Added budget math comments and a spike detector that cancels diffusion and emits telemetry (kv.diffusion_spike). See second commit.

release_notes: Added an optional anticipatory KV diffusion seeding layer and a decode gang scheduler to reduce prefill misses and kernel thrash. Both features are feature-flag gated; operators can tune kv.diffusion.* and scheduler.gang_size. Expected improvements for interactive mixed-burst workloads: lower prefill miss-rate and reduced tail latency.
performance_summary: Lab results (seq=64 mixed-interactive trace): median E2E latency -7.6%, p95 -11.2%, prefill miss-rate -36% on high-locality traces. Diffusion CPU overhead measured at <1.8% of runtime in steady state for default budget settings.
files_modified_high_level: Introduce kv diffusion module that seeds hot keys asynchronously with a bounded budget
Add gang scheduler to co-schedule decode tasks with overlapping kernel/kv footprints
Expose runtime flags for diffusion budget and gang size and add telemetry for diffusion hits and spike events
Add tests, bench harness and docs for configuration and rollout
